metadata.name: Acute tonsillitis
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - recognise peritonsillar abscess and airway red flags
metadata.severity: Usually mild and self-limiting; recurrent disease affects quality of life

overview.short_description: Acute inflammation of the tonsils, usually viral, presenting with sore throat, painful swallowing, fever and tonsillar swelling; overlaps with pharyngitis.
overview.detailed_description: Acute tonsillitis and pharyngitis are managed as one clinical problem ('acute sore throat'). Most cases are viral and self-limiting; group A Streptococcus is the main treatable bacterial cause. Scoring (Centor/FeverPAIN) guides antibiotic decisions. Recurrent, frequent, well-documented episodes may warrant ENT referral for tonsillectomy.
overview.pathophysiology: Viral or bacterial infection of tonsillar tissue produces inflammation, exudate and reactive lymphadenopathy; marked unilateral swelling suggests peritonsillar abscess.
overview.etiology: Mostly respiratory viruses (including EBV); bacterial mainly group A Streptococcus.
overview.natural_history: Most resolve within about a week; some patients have recurrent episodes.

prevalence.value: Very common, especially in children and young adults.

mortality.value: Negligible; serious outcomes only via rare airway/deep-space or rheumatic complications.

epidemiology.age_groups: Children and young adults most affected.

symptoms.symptom: Unilateral severe pain, trismus, muffled voice (quinsy)

negative_findings.why_important: Favours viral cause and lowers streptococcal probability

negative_findings.finding: No trismus, uvular deviation, drooling, or stridor

history_questions.question: Do you have a cough and cold symptoms?
How many documented episodes have you had this year and in prior years?
history_questions.why_ask: Assesses tonsillectomy criteria (e.g., >=7 in 1 year, >=5/year for 2 years, >=3/year for 3 years)

history_questions.question: Any one-sided severe pain, trismus, drooling, or breathing difficulty?
Young adult with prolonged symptoms and marked fatigue?
On carbimazole/clozapine or immunosuppressed?
history_questions.why_ask: Consider agranulocytosis if severe sore throat + fever

physical_examination.expected_finding: Enlarged, erythematous tonsils +/- exudate; check symmetry (quinsy)

physical_examination.examination: Abdomen for splenomegaly if EBV suspected
physical_examination.expected_finding: May be enlarged in glandular fever

laboratory_tests.indication: Higher-probability cases where testing is used

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Flexible laryngoscopy by ENT if airway concern
other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Only if malignancy suspected (persistent unilateral tonsillar enlargement/ulcer)
other_diagnostic_tests.culture: Throat swab for GAS as above

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Clinical diagnosis of acute sore throat/tonsillitis; use Centor/McIsaac or FeverPAIN to estimate streptococcal probability and guide antibiotics.

diagnostic_scores.value: Centor and FeverPAIN as for pharyngitis; higher scores favour streptococcal cause.

cutoff_values.value: Centor >=3 or FeverPAIN >=4 favour antibiotics/testing (NICE NG84). Tonsillectomy (SIGN/ENT-UK): documented sore throats due to tonsillitis with disabling frequency (e.g., >=7 in the preceding year, or >=5/year for 2 years, or >=3/year for 3 years).

differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Do you have a cough and runny nose?

differential_diagnosis.differences: No cough, higher fever, tender nodes, higher score
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Do you have a cough? (absence favours strep)

differential_diagnosis.differences: Young adult, prolonged, marked fatigue, splenomegaly
differential_diagnosis.red_flags: Splenic rupture; airway obstruction; amoxicillin rash
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Very tired for more than a week with big glands?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Unilateral, trismus, muffled voice, uvular deviation
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is it one-sided with difficulty opening your mouth?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Persistent unilateral enlargement/ulcer, older/smoker, weight loss
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Has one tonsil been enlarged/ulcerated for weeks?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a cough and cold symptoms with the sore throat?
Is the pain one-sided with trismus or a muffled voice?

next_best_question.current_situation: Acute tonsillitis, no airway red flags
next_best_question.question: Do you have cough/cold symptoms, and how many episodes have you had this year?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Viral features -> avoid antibiotics; high score -> antibiotics/testing; frequent recurrence -> ENT referral for tonsillectomy assessment

next_best_test.why: Confirm strep or diagnose glandular fever

red_flags.finding: Stridor, drooling, or difficulty breathing/swallowing saliva
red_flags.immediate_action: Airway emergency - urgent ENT/anaesthetics; do not examine throat aggressively

red_flags.finding: Unilateral severe pain, trismus, muffled voice, uvular deviation
Severe sore throat + fever on carbimazole/clozapine or immunosuppressed

red_flags.immediate_action: Urgent ENT referral to exclude malignancy

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Suspected quinsy/deep-space infection; persistent unilateral tonsillar mass (cancer pathway).

initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Paracetamol; NSAID; Phenoxymethylpenicillin; Macrolide. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG84.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Fluids, rest, soothing drinks; stay home while febrile.
initial_management.follow_up: Safety-net for airway/quinsy signs; document episodes for possible tonsillectomy assessment.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Symptomatic relief; antibiotics only for higher-probability streptococcal cases or systemically unwell (phenoxymethylpenicillin first-line; macrolide if penicillin-allergic; AVOID amoxicillin if EBV possible). Consider delayed prescribing.

patient_education.home_advice: Tonsillitis is usually a viral throat infection that settles within a week. Painkillers and fluids help; antibiotics are only needed for some bacterial cases. Get urgent help if you have trouble breathing or swallowing saliva, drooling, a muffled voice, or one-sided severe pain with difficulty opening your mouth.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: التهاب اللوزتين غالباً عدوى فيروسية تزول خلال أسبوع. تفيد مسكّنات الألم والسوائل، والمضادات الحيوية تلزم فقط في بعض الحالات البكتيرية. اطلب المساعدة العاجلة إذا صعُب التنفّس أو بلع الريق، أو سال اللعاب، أو تغيّر الصوت، أو حدث ألم شديد في جانب واحد مع صعوبة فتح الفم.
patient_education.prevention: Hand hygiene; avoid close contact while infectious.
patient_education.warning_signs: Difficulty breathing/swallowing saliva, drooling, muffled voice, one-sided severe pain with trismus, or a persistently enlarged single tonsil.

evidence.evidence_level: High for scoring-guided antibiotics; tonsillectomy benefit for well-selected recurrent cases.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG84; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE NG84, SIGN/ENT-UK for tonsillectomy.
